quorum.kill_rule: a claim survives when the last round to judge it confirmed it and the author re-measured it; any measured refutation was acted on before the next round
refuted_claims: [r1] The bind-only probe keeps directed broadcasts remote. — REFUTED: false — Linux lets a UDP socket bind a subnet's directed broadcast. Both r1 lanes measured 192.168.1.255, 10.42.0.255, 172.17.255.255 and 127.255.255.255 classified local at 16b144b7. Fixed in abd16b12 by requiring `connect` to succeed as well (`src/transport/local_iface.rs:49`), which refuses a broadcast destination without SO_BROADCAST.

[r1] The probe judges ::ffff:a.b.c.d under the right sysctl. — REFUTED: false at 16b144b7 — an IPv4-mapped literal read the IPv6 ip_nonlocal_bind while the kernel binds it through the IPv4 stack. Fixed in abd16b12 by `probe_target` folding with `to_canonical` (`src/transport/local_iface.rs:28`), pinned by `src/transport/tests_local_iface.rs:115`.

[r1] The route-source tests always measure something. — REFUTED: false — with no IPv4 route they return early and assert nothing, so on a network-less runner the fix had no discriminating test. abd16b12 added the 127.0.0.2 dispatch test at `tests/falsification_is_local_addr_interface.rs:79`, which needs no network on Linux.

[r2] The probe is correct on every platform forjar runs on. — REFUTED: unbacked — the broadcast refusal rests on Linux `connect` semantics and nobody measured macOS. 28519ba6 gates the probe to Linux (`src/transport/local_iface.rs:46`), so elsewhere it declines to SSH, the behaviour before it existed.

[r2] An unreadable sysctl declines the probe, as the module doc says. — REFUTED: false at abd16b12 — an unreadable /proc/sys/net read counted as disabled, so the probe answered. Found by the author while fixing r2; 28519ba6 makes a failed read count as enabled (`src/transport/local_iface.rs:69`).

[r2] Every address a local interface holds is recognised. — REFUTED: false for IPv6 link-local — fe80:: cannot be bound without a scope id and a scoped literal does not parse as an IpAddr. Narrowed and documented as a false negative, never a false positive, and pinned by `src/transport/tests_local_iface.rs:141`, which reads a real scope-20 row from /proc/net/if_inet6.

[r2] Any 127/8 address is local on Linux. — REFUTED: false for 127.255.255.255, lo's broadcast. This was the brief's wording, not the code's: the code and `tests/falsification_is_local_addr_interface.rs:104` already assert 127.255.255.255 remote. The comment that repeated the wording was corrected in 984fb9b7.

[r4] The test suite passes off Linux with the fix in place. — REFUTED: false at 984fb9b7 — Gemini found `test_local_iface_nonlocal_bind_never_claims_local` asserting `ip_held_locally(127.0.0.1, false)` on every platform while the probe declines off Linux, so it would panic on macOS and contradict the off-Linux test. Every Claude seat ran on Linux and missed it. c72ccb3a gates that assertion to Linux (`src/transport/tests_local_iface.rs:69`).

[r4] The unreadable-sysctl decline and the v4/v6 sysctl choice are pinned by tests. — REFUTED: false at 984fb9b7 — Gemini showed that mutating `map_or(true, …)` to `map_or(false, …)`, or swapping the two sysctl paths, left every test green. c72ccb3a splits the read into `nonlocal_bind_path` and `nonlocal_bind_read` and pins each (`src/transport/tests_local_iface.rs:81`, `src/transport/tests_local_iface.rs:90`); both mutations were measured red.
quorum.divergence: Rounds 1–3 were a same-family (Claude sonnet + haiku) quorum, recorded as one. r2 split 2 PASS / 1 FAIL (haiku); r3 was 3/3 PASS. The cross-family Gemini lane then FAILED r4 on a defect every Claude seat missed because all ran on Linux — an un-gated assertion that panics off Linux — and PASSED r5 after the fix.

crux.verdict: None of the four infers local from the interfaces the controller holds; each needs an explicit connection setting or a localhost spelling. forjar goes further by asking the kernel (bind+connect, Linux only) and declines to SSH, the field default, wherever it cannot answer. The cost — a held address bypasses ssh-config remaps and the machine user/ssh_key — is documented in the module doc and is the trust forjar already extends to loopback spellings and /etc/hostname.
